sources.cite: Microsoft Learn, SAP workloads on Azure: planning and deployment guide
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-17. Relevant text: 'The configuring of network virtual appliances in the communication path between the SAP application layer and the DBMS layer ... isn't supported'; 'Network virtual appliances in communication paths can easily double the network latency between two communication partners'; 'The restriction doesn't include ASG and NSG rules if the ASG and NSG rules allow a direct communication path'; the path between application servers and DBMS 'must be a direct path'; accelerated networking should be confirmed on every SAP VM; proximity placement groups only 'when default placement doesn't meet network roundtrip requirements'. The page gives no latency threshold and does not describe niping; SAP's niping tool for latency measurement is named in a Microsoft Learn training unit seen as a search result on 2026-11-17 (to verify).

brief.situation: You are the SAP Basis and Azure engineer for Ridgeway Components, a fictional manufacturer that moved its ERP system to Azure last weekend. Since this morning, dialog response times have doubled and users report slow screens. The month-end closing jobs start at 09:30 and cannot run like this. The application servers sit in subnet snet-sap-app and the database in snet-sap-db of the same virtual network.
handover: Network security groups on both subnets allow only the ports the system needs between the two.
On Friday the security team raised CHG-5120 to 'inspect east-west traffic'.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows the application server, its route table, the hub firewall appliance and the database.
Each command takes a minute or two; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

source.note: The month-end closing jobs start at 09:30, 50 minutes after the report.

writeup.question: For the record: what slowed the database calls, what you changed, and how the path stays controlled.

parts.label: What
parts.criteria: Measures the round trip and finds the route that adds the hop.
parts.modelAnswer: niping showed 0.92 ms against a 0.34 ms baseline, and the effective routes showed a user route for 10.30.2.0/24 to the firewall appliance, added Friday by CHG-5120. Accelerated networking was on and both VMs were in zone 1.

parts.label: Change
parts.criteria: Removes only that route, keeping internet egress through the firewall.
parts.modelAnswer: Deleted the to-db route, so the virtual network's direct route carries database traffic again; the 0.0.0.0/0 route to the firewall stays. An appliance between the SAP application and database layers is not supported and can double latency.

parts.label: Control
parts.criteria: Keeps the path restricted without an appliance and tells the change owner.
parts.modelAnswer: NSG rules on both subnets still allow only the needed ports, which the support statement permits; niping is back to 0.35 ms, and CHG-5120's owners have the reason and the alternative (NSG flow logs).

egressBypass.headline: Faster, and uninspected
egressBypass.body: Only the route for the database subnet was the problem. Removing it keeps the default route through the firewall; detaching the table removes both.

redeployed.headline: Placement was not the problem
redeployed.body: Both VMs were already in one zone. A proximity placement group is for when default placement misses the round-trip requirement; here an appliance in the path doubled it.

closeSlow.headline: The close ran slow
closeSlow.body: Bigger VMs wait on the same round trips. niping and the NIC's effective routes find the extra hop in two commands.

direct.headline: Good: a direct path, still controlled
direct.body: You measured before changing anything, ruled out accelerated networking and placement, removed only the route that broke the support statement, kept egress through the firewall, and explained it to the change owner.

gaps.headline: Restored, with gaps
gaps.body: The criteria show what was left: the measurement, the routes, the check afterward, telling CHG-5120's owners, or a resize that did nothing.

time_up.headline: Time up
time_up.body: No record was written before the run's hard limit.

scoring.modelReasoning: The round trip from the application server to the database nearly tripled, and the NIC's effective routes show a user route for the database subnet sending every call through the firewall appliance, added by Friday's change. Accelerated networking is on and both VMs share a zone, so a resize or a proximity placement group would not help. An appliance between the SAP application and database layers is not a supported configuration and can double latency; NSG rules that allow a direct path are allowed. Remove only that route, keep the default route through the firewall, confirm the round trip with niping, and tell the change owner why, with NSG flow logs as a way to see the traffic.
